name: Benjamini–Yekutieli false discovery control
definition: For ordered valid p-values p_(1)≤…≤p_(m), let H_m=Σ_(j=1)^m 1/j and q∈(0,1). Set k=max({0}∪{i:p_(i)≤i q/(m H_m)}); reject the first k hypotheses.
variables: m positive number of hypotheses; p_(i) sorted p-values; H_m harmonic sum; q target false discovery rate; k rejection count
assumptions: Prespecified family of valid super-uniform null p-values; arbitrary dependence allowed under the theorem
limitations: Conservative for large families; invalid or adaptively selected p-values can invalidate guarantees
failure_conditions: Incomplete test family or invalid null p-values
computation: Sort p-values and scan the harmonic-adjusted thresholds; O(m log m)

source.citation: Benjamini and Yekutieli (2001), The control of the false discovery rate in multiple testing under dependency, Theorem 1.3; SciPy false_discovery_control documentation: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.false_discovery_control.html

application: Audit multiplicity in a prespecified family of scientific comparisons on permitted development data
required_inputs: Complete prespecified family of valid hypothesis-test p-values and target q
incompatible_methods: Post hoc omission of unsuccessful tests
mechanism_note: Harmonic adjustment changes the rejection threshold under arbitrary dependence; not an additional independent test of the same hypothesis.

name: One-dimensional energy distance
definition: D(P,Q)=[2E|X−Y|−E|X−X′|−E|Y−Y′|]^(1/2), where X,X′ independently follow P and Y,Y′ independently follow Q, with all four draws independent.
variables: P,Q real-valued distributions; X,X′,Y,Y′ independent draws; D nonnegative distance
assumptions: Finite first absolute moments; comparable measurement units; empirical plug-in uses empirical product distributions
limitations: Magnitude depends on measurement scale; distance alone is not a significance test and does not establish causality
failure_conditions: Incompatible measurement scales or undefined first moments
computation: Compute weighted pairwise absolute differences under empirical distributions, including within-sample diagonal terms

source.citation: SciPy maintainers, energy_distance API, mathematical definition and references. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.energy_distance.html

name: Two-sample Cramér–von Mises test
definition: T=(nm/(n+m))∫[F_n(x)−G_m(x)]² dH_(n+m)(x), with H_(n+m)=(nF_n+mG_m)/(n+m), evaluated for continuous distributions without ties.
variables: F_n,G_m empirical distribution functions, n,m positive sample sizes, H pooled empirical CDF, T discrepancy statistic
assumptions: Independent samples and independent observations within samples from continuous distributions under the usual null; the stated statistic assumes no ties
limitations: Dependent sequences require a separately justified test; discrete data and ties need an appropriate rank and null-distribution treatment
computation: Sort pooled observations and sum squared CDF differences weighted by pooled empirical mass; compute a valid null reference separately

source.citation: SciPy maintainers, cramervonmises_2samp API and references. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.cramervonmises_2samp.html

application: Investigate whether comparable independent historical samples have the same distribution
required_inputs: Two independent authorised development samples of a comparable continuous measurement
mechanism_note: Two empirical distributions are compared, unlike the one-sample test against a specified theoretical CDF.
